title: Add capturable support to Adagrad
body:

## Issue

Fixes #118715

## Summary

I reviewed the implementation line by line and authorized submission after reviewing the baseline, lint, compiled optimizer, CUDA graph, CPU/CUDA correctness, and dual RTX 3090 benchmark evidence. I understand the change and take responsibility for it.

> **AI assistance disclosure:** AI tools assisted with the implementation and this draft description. The contributor reviewed and approved both.
>
> This adds a capturable option to Adagrad, initializes optimizer state lazily on the appropriate device, and keeps the single-tensor and foreach update paths on-device during graph capture. It adds optimizer database coverage, CUDA graph tests, checkpoint migration coverage, lazy-module coverage, and compiled optimizer coverage. The targeted Adagrad optimizer suite passed 150 tests with 24 skips. CUDA graph, checkpoint, and representative compiled optimizer tests passed independently on two RTX 3090 GPUs. For a 64 x 4096 FP32 microbenchmark, graph replay reduced median single-tensor step time from 13.101 ms to 0.842 ms on GPU 0 and from 13.010 ms to 0.841 ms on GPU 1; foreach decreased from 3.028 ms to 0.112 ms and from 3.070 ms to 0.112 ms, respectively. Eager sparse behavior remains covered, but CUDA graph capture of uncoalesced sparse gradients remains unsupported because the existing CUDA COO coalesce() path synchronizes with the host.

## Checklist

- [ ] Passes lint (spin fixlint); targeted FLAKE8, PYFMT, RUFF, CODESPELL, NEWLINE, and PYREFLY passed
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [x] Updated documentation (not applicable; the new argument uses the shared optimizer documentation)
- [x] Included benchmark results

## BC-breaking?

No.
